scientific_scope.statement: For G = C_2^4 (naturals below 16 under XOR, certified isomorphic to (Z/2)^4 with coordinatewise addition): rank 4 >= 2; D(G) = 5 in the source's sense (every sequence over G of length >= 5 has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence, by a pruned exhaustive kernel search proved sound; [1,2,4,8] has none; 5 is the unique value meeting the definition); D*(G) = 1 + 4(2-1) = 5; k = 2 > 0; exp(G) = 2 <= D-k = 3 <= D; 2(D-k) >= D+1 (with equality); and it is NOT the case that some positive l <= 7 has every length-l sequence over G containing a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of length <= 3. Indeed for every l <= 8 the first l terms of [8,...,15] are a sequence of length exactly l with no such subsequence, so s_{<=3}(G) >= 9 > 7 = D + k. Also the negation of the printed conjecture specialised to this group (all admissible k, both branches).
scientific_scope.outcome_scope: refutes Conjecture 6.2 of arXiv:2506.21383v1 AS PRINTED (a universal statement over groups and k, refuted by the single instance G = C_2^4, k = 2 with every hypothesis certified). It does not touch the conjecture with C_2^4 excluded, as Theorem 1.11 and Conjecture 6.1 of the same paper do exclude it.
binding_points: the instance sits exactly at the threshold D-k = 3 = (D+1)/2; the source prints '>=' in the upper branch and '<' in the lower, and its own confirming examples C_3^3 and C_5^3 satisfy the equality case only in the upper branch; under a strict '>' reading the instance would fall in the (true) lower branch and nothing would be refuted (at_threshold; readings_check.out R4, R7)

Conjecture 6.2 as printed does not exclude C_2^4, while Theorem 1.11 and Conjecture 6.1 of the same paper do; importing that exclusion removes the refutation, which is why the case is a source-internal inconsistency of the printed statement

s_{<=k}(G) is defined with 'each sequence of length l' (exactly l), so s_{<=3}(G) <= 7 is refuted only by free sequences of EVERY length 1..7: short_lower gives every l <= 8; the 'length at least l' variant is refuted too (not_shortPropGe)

sequences are lists and subsequences are List.Sublist. The source (PDF p. 4) takes sequences in the free abelian monoid F(G) and calls T a subsequence of S when v_g(S) >= v_g(T) for all g, that is, a sub-multiset; for every list S the sub-multisets of S are exactly the contents of the sublists of S and the sum does not depend on order, so the list model is equivalent for positive and negative statements alike (adversarial review, section 2). The earlier, narrower reason also holds: both free witnesses are strictly increasing lists, so every sub-multiset is a sublist

the carrier is C_2^4 by group_is_C2_pow_4 (XOR is coordinatewise addition mod 2 on four binary digits, bijectively); rank, exponent and D* are computed from the invariant-factor list [2,2,2,2] read off that direct-sum form, not from a formalised structure theorem

the inconsistency is visible inside the abstract alone: it conjectures k_G = (D(G)+1)/2 for all G with r(G) >= 2 and D(G) = D*(G), and says k_G <= D(G) - 2 is proved for all G with r(G) >= 2 'except C_2^3 and C_2^4'; at C_2^4 both come down to s_{<=3}(G) <= 7 (adversarial review, section 3; quoted in BINDING.md)
scientific_scope.not_claimed: the exact value s_{<=3}(C_2^4) = 9 (only the lower bound >= 9 is certified; an ordered kernel search for the upper bound has 1,658,386 nodes against 22,906 for the Davenport search and was not attempted); anything about other groups or other k; novelty (the source states both values itself); that no later arXiv version corrects the statement (v1 was the only version listed on 2026-09-19)
